title: staging-network-scan-and-ops-requirements
content:
Context:
This is a field-oriented notes + lightweight runbook used after our 2024-08-12 customer workshop with NeuroFrame Health (pseudonym). Goal: capture the constraints discovered during the on-prem staging network scan, lay out minimal operational requirements for an air-gapped/private deployment POC, and surface outstanding technical questions for the engineering/ops teams. Intended audience: SEs, infra engineers, SRE, and customer IT stakeholders.

Executive summary (short):
- Customer environment is a segmented clinical research site with an isolated staging VLAN that can reach limited internal services but has no routable internet.
- Required delivery: containerized inference service + local control plane (management API) delivered as signed offline artifact with deterministic install steps.
- Key blockers: A) secure out-of-band package transport for initial install and future patches; B) KMS integration constraints (HSM only on FIPS boundary, limited PKI cert issuance); C) monitoring/alerting pipeline needs tethered push model.

Who we talked to (workshop):
- NeuroFrame: Rachel Park (IT Ops), Tom Alvarez (Network), Priya Menon (Security), Dr. Anil Rao (Research lead)
- Redwood: Maya Singh (SE lead), Aiden Chen (deploy engineer), Sofia Martinez (solutions PM)

Site summary / constraints discovered during scan:
- Physical: 2x 42U racks available in staging, power per rack: 2x 20A PDUs (NEMA L6-20 in RM 214); no dedicated cold aisle. Raised-floor HVAC rated to 5kW/rack but site policy limits to 3kW/rack without change requests.
- Network: VLANed staging network (172.22.120.0/24) behind a firewall with deny-by-default. No outbound internet. DNS is internal-only (ns-stg.local) and DHCP is managed centrally.
- Storage: Network-attached storage provided via NFSv4 with AES-GCM encryption at rest; export only to specific hosts. No object storage available.
- Identity: Corporate AD (Azure AD Connect hybrid) but AD admins do not allow cross-domain trust for vendor accounts. Customer prefers certificate-based service identity with mTLS.
- Security/compliance: Must run on FIPS-validated crypto modules for any key handling. Vulnerability scanning requires central scanning window (Tues 0100-0300) and patching needs sign-off by security.

Minimal functional requirements (POC scope):
1) Inference runtime (containerized) that can run on a single dedicated GPU node (NVIDIA A40 confirmed available). Must support model pinning and local KV-cache.
2) Local control plane to manage model versions, rollout policies, and observability agents. Expose only internal API endpoints (no public endpoints).
3) Offline installation artifacts: signed tarball with image layers + sha256 manifest + signature bundle. Support USB and air-gapped scp via jump host.
4) Local metrics/alerting: Prometheus-compatible metrics pushed to an internal pushgateway; optionally local Prometheus + Grafana with no external telemetry.
5) Secure key storage: integration with on-prem HSM (customer uses Thales Luna SA) or, short-term, sealed software keystores with strict ACLs.
6) Operational hooks: health check endpoints, graceful shutdown, and automated disk cleanup for model cache.

Network / firewall rules (customer-provided):
- Ingress: allow management traffic from staging-admin jump host (10.10.3.5/32) to control-plane API on TCP 8443.
- Egress: minimal — allow NTP to internal NTP servers (UDP 123), DNS to ns-stg.local (TCP/UDP 53), and NFS to storage nodes on ports 2049/tcp.
- No outbound HTTPS to internet; any outbound to external registries must be via airgap process.
- mTLS required for inter-service RPC; CA certs must be provisioned during install.

Packaging and delivery model (recommended):
- Primary: signed OCI artifact bundle exported as a tar.gz (images + charts + manifests). Bundle integrity verified by Redwood install utility using embedded public key (customer to trust Redwood public key via fingerprint exchange).
- Transport: initial delivery via encrypted external USB delivered to on-site security, then mounted on jump host for scp to staging network. Future patches delivered same way or via physically transported update server.
- Verification: installer computes sha256 checksums and verifies signature using OpenSSL FIPS mode.

KMS/HSM notes and constraints:
- Customer insists all model encryption keys must reside in HSM; private key usage for signing the runtime binary must be in HSM.
- We need to validate Redwood's ability to issue keys that can be imported or referenced by Luna SA. Two options: 1) Redwood provides sealed keys; customer imports into HSM (operational friction). 2) Use HSM-backed PKCS#11 provider from customer side and Redwood calls the provider via a secure sidecar in the network (requires local integration work).
- Action: schedule a Luna SA POC session with customer security and our security engineer (Aiden) to validate PKCS#11 flow.

Observability and support model:
- Monitoring should be push-first: local agent (prom-pushgateway) pushes metrics to an internal aggregator. For support, Redwood support team will request temporary support sessions that the customer must create via a Bastion jump host. No permanent backchannels allowed.
- Logs: store locally for 90 days; export to customer SIEM via file transfer. We must provide log rotation and encrypted-at-rest storage paths.

Operational runbook (POC-level):
- Pre-install checklist: verify rack space, confirm PDU cables, validate GPU driver compat (NVIDIA 510+), collect CA certs and jump-host credentials, receive signed bundle on USB.
- Install steps (high level): 1. copy bundle to jump host, 2. run installer with --offline --verify-signature, 3. install runtime and control-plane containers, 4. run smoke tests (see tests below), 5. provision models from local model-store manifest.
- Smoke tests: start runtime with sample model, run 100 sample inference requests (synthetic) with latency < 200ms p50, verify model pinning and rollback by toggling control plane version.
- Rollback: have known-good image tags and scripts to revert control plane and runtime.

Security and patching cadence:
- Patches must be delivered as signed bundles. Customer patch window Tuesdays 0100-0300; emergency patches flagged and require manual signoff.
- Vulnerability scanning: central scanner will run weekly; we must provide SBOM for all components and documented CVE response plan.

Acceptance criteria for POC:
- Successfully provisioned inference runtime and control plane in staging VLAN with no outbound internet usage.
- Model serving validated with golden test set (accuracy within expected delta) and latency confirmed under SLOs (p50 < 200ms).
- Observability metrics visible in internal Grafana and alerts firing to internal PagerDuty test integration.
- Documented install + rollback executed by customer Ops without Redwood SSH access (Redwood guidance only).

Outstanding questions / decisions needed (open items):
- Q1: Can customer import Redwood public keys into their HSM, or do we need to support PKCS#11 direct calls from our control plane? (Owner: Aiden)
- Q2: Is 3kW/rack the hard limit for this POC or can we get temporary HVAC uplift for GPU runs? (Owner: Rachel)
- Q3: Which internal NFS export will hold the model blobs and what are throughput limits? (Owner: Tom)
- Q4: Confirm legal for data residency / telemetry handshake (Owner: Sofia, Legal).

Next steps / action items (short):
- Aiden: schedule Luna SA integration lab (target 2024-08-26).
- Maya: prepare signed OCI bundle generation docs + sample installer flags (2024-08-20).
- Tom/Rachel: email network team to whitelist jump host and provide NFS export details (2024-08-18).
- Sofia: raise ENG-4823 and attach SBOM template + compliance checklist (2024-08-19).

Appendix: quick checklist for field engineer deploying the POC:
- Verify jump-host credentials and ACLs
- Bring USB with signed bundle (hash printed on paper)
- Confirm GPU driver version + nvidia-smi output
- Confirm firewall rules and DNS resolution to control-plane hostnames
- Collect HSM/APIs contact and schedule time with customer security

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep installer as idempotent as possible; customers will rerun.
- Consider building a tiny "verification shim" that runs offline regression tests against the model to reduce back-and-forth.
- Explore adding a small local web UI for operators to review logs/metrics without CLI.

End of notes.
